To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ANNs have been applied in a variety of auditing domains, but that the application of ANNs has not been studied in the AR process.
ANN‐applications in auditing have been conducted in various domains, but there are no studies in the AR process.
ANN‐based auditing applications have been used to predict the likelihood that the financial statements are materially misstated and to identify misstated financial statements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether ANNs could serve AR procedures.
the question whether ANNs have potential in the analytical review process.
the question: what are the most relevant findings in the field of ANN‐applications in auditing, and how can they be used in analytical review procedures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ANNs have the potential to improve analytical reviews.
ANNs have a promising potential to support the AR‐process.
ANNs are not ready to be implemented in analytical review.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ANNs could be a valuable addition to the AR‐toolbox of auditors.
ANNs are a powerful tool to improve analytical review procedures.
ANNs have the potential to support AR procedures and that the most influential contributions are the ones that use data sets that represent the AR process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ANNs could be applied in the AR process to increase its efficiency.
the potential of ANN in auditing is not yet fully exploited.
ANNs have great potential to be used as an analytical tool to improve the quality of the analytical review (and other) procedures.
